## Introduction to environment control
A coding environment usually includes all the packages and software tools with specific version that you use for coding. Environment control is extremely important for the reproducibility of data analysis because using a different version of certain package could lead to changes in results or even corrupt the whole analysis pipeline. Based on this fact, it is always recommended to set up a new environment first at the start of a project and put all the analysis in the same environment.

## Pixi: a tool for environment control
Pixi is a useful tool to help create a coding environment (which exists as a folder) and install packages we need in this environment.

### 1. Installation
- Download the installation script from pixi website and run.
- Remember to source the start up file to update `~/.bashrc` file so that you can use pixi commands.
```{bash}
#| eval: false

curl -fsSL https://pixi.sh/install.sh | sh

source ~/.bashrc # in Linux
source ~/.zshrc # in Mac
```

### 2. Set up evironment
- A folder `name_environment_folder` will be created with this command line. All the operation under this folder will share the same coding environment. 
- Flag `-c` indicates channels which we download and install dependencies (or packages) from. Note that `conda-forge` must be placed before `bioconda`.
```{bash}
#| eval: false
pixi init name_environment_folder -c conda-forge -c bioconda
```

#### 2.1 Information about a pixi environment
- A `pixi.toml` file is created when we first set up the environment, which includes the basic information about the environment. 
- Packages installed in this environment are recorded in `[dependencies]` of the file.
- The following is an example of this file:
```{bash}
#| eval: false
[workspace]
channels = ["conda-forge", "bioconda"]
name = "pixi_training"
platforms = ["linux-64"]
version = "0.1.0"

[tasks]

[dependencies]
quarto = ">=1.8.25,<2"
```

#### 2.2 Add dependencies
- Take installing Quarto as an example, a `pixi.lock` file will be create to record the process of installation.
- Dependencies are installed in `.pixi/envs` under environment folder.
```{bash}
#| eval: false
pixi add quarto
```

### 3. Run pixi
#### 3.1 Basic command
- We can run pixi command directly:
```{bash}
#| eval: false

pixi run quarto --help
```
- or we can start up a shell (it is like activating the evironment) so that we can run commands in a tranditional way without `pixi run`:
```{bash}
#| eval: false

pixi shell # activate environment
quarto --help # run normal command without pixi run
exit # quit
```

#### 3.2 Example: Run fastqc in pixi environment
- First set up pixi environment:
```{bash}
#| eval: false

pixi init -c conda-forge -c bioconda
pixi add fastqc
pixi run fastqc --help
```

- Run in **SLURM** (Simple Linux Utility for Resource Management) job scheduling system:
```{bash}
#| eval: false

# Basic usage
srun -A project_ID -t 30:00 -n 1 <tool options and commands>

# Adapt for fastqc
srun -A project_ID -t 15:00 -n 1 fastqc --noextract -o fastqc data/sample_1.fastq.gz data/sample_2.fastq.gz 
```
- Note that `project_ID` indicate the project on server which you are a member of.

- Check the project you are a member of:
```{bash}
#| eval: false

projinfo
```

- Run in batch by submitting a `fastqc.sh` script. Here is an example of the script:
```{bash}
#| eval: false

#! /bin/bash -l
#SBATCH -A project_ID
#SBATCH -t 30:00
#SBATCH -n 1

fastqc -o ../fastqc --noextract ../data/*fastq.gz
```

- Use `sbatch` to run the script:
```{bash}
#| eval: false

sbatch fastqc.sh 
```

- Check your job with:
```{bash}
#| eval: false

squeue -u <user-name>
```

### 4. Container
#### 4.1 Introduction to Container
Even if we have very convenitent tools to manage our own coding environment, problems could still exist when we try to reproduce analysis of other researchers due to conflicts in program version, software dependencies and operating systems, etc.

- **Container** provides a solution to this kind of problem. Container. Containers are **stand-alone** pieces of software that require a container management tool to run. They are build and exchanged as **container images that specify the contents of the container**, such as the operating system, all dependencies, and software in an isolated environment. The container management tool then takes the images and build the container. These management tools can be run on all operating systems, and since **the container has the operating system within it**, it will run the same in all environments. Container images are easily portable and immutable, so they are stable over time.

- Programs to run Containers: [Docker](https://www.docker.com), [Apptainer](https://apptainer.org), [Podman](https://podman.io).

- Websties for downloading Containers: [Dockerhub](https://hub.docker.com), [Seqera](https://seqera.io/containers/).

#### 4.2 Run Container
- Download Container images:
```{bash}
#| eval: false

# from Dockerhub
apptainer pull vcftools_0.1.16-1.sif docker://biocontainers/vcftools:v0.1.16-1-deb_cv1

# from Seqera
apptainer pull vcftools_0.1.17.sif oras://community.wave.seqera.io/library/vcftools:0.1.17--b541aa8d9f9213f9
```

- Run Container:
```{bash}
#| eval: false

apptainer exec vcftools_0.1.17.sif vcftools --version
```

- Run Container with sbatch:
```{bash}
#| eval: false

#! /bin/bash -l
#SBATCH -A project_ID
#SBATCH -t 30:00
#SBATCH -n 1

apptainer exec container_image.sif fastqc -o . --noextract ../data/*fastq.gz
```
